title: env.sandbox.call.export result
description: The golden record that would be written, and whether it was.

hex.description: Lowercase hex. A JSON document cannot carry raw bytes, and a seed is part of the record a caller diffs, so it has to be spellable.

from.description: The range this seed copied, when the recipe named one rather than the bytes. Absent for a seed spelled out as hex — which is what tells a reader that a seed was the image's own bytes rather than a string somebody typed.

source.description: The source copied from. Absent means the image being run.

sha256.description: The digest of the file this range was replayed from, present only for an artifact seed and checked before the routine ran. This is what tells the two apart: a `from` with no source is a range of the image the record already pins, while an artifact is a file nothing else in the record mentions.

stop.description: Why the run stopped. Every variant is a distinct fact about the code, not a shade of failure.

offset.description: The signed library-vector offset. Naming it against an fd table is the frontend's, because the tables are its configuration.

returned.description: Whether the routine returned cleanly, which is the one thing a caller checks before trusting the outputs.

changed_memory.description: Every run of memory the routine changed, excluding the stack. The stack is scratch, and including it would make every record differ from every other for reasons that say nothing about the routine.

hex.description: Lowercase hex. A JSON document cannot carry raw bytes, and a seed is part of the record a caller diffs, so it has to be spellable.

trace.description: The per-instruction trace, capped. Empty unless `trace` was asked for: a golden record is about inputs and outputs, and a trace kept by default would make two runs with identical outputs produce records that differ.

trace_total.description: Rows the call produced before the cap. Non-zero even without `trace` when a watched range forced recording, because that is what was run.

watch_events_total.description: Accesses that matched a watched range, counted across the whole run. Not the same as the number of watch_hits the trace carries: the trace is capped in rows, retention is capped in events, and an attached device can make one instruction produce more matching accesses than a run makes instructions. This is the true total either way.

watch_events_truncated.description: Whether more accesses matched than were retained, so the watch_hits on the trace rows are a prefix rather than the whole set.

exported_regions.description: Every range of final memory the recipe named, digested rather than carried. A recipe plus a digest reproduces the bytes and is bounded; the bytes themselves are what `env.sandbox.call.export` writes.

capture_note.description: What produced these bytes, as one sentence, for `project.edit`'s `register_capture` to record. Composed here rather than by whoever registers it: a capture is bytes no one can obtain again, so this note is the only provenance they will ever have, and a person writing it from memory writes prose that happens to be true. Deterministic — the same recipe over the same bytes composes the same sentence.

interrupts_delivered.description: Every scheduled interrupt that was delivered, in order, capped at 256. A run whose outcome depended on a handler running has to say that it ran: an initialization that only completes because a flag was cleared is not reproducible from a record that does not mention the clearing.

index.description: Which entry of the request's schedule delivered.

handler.description: The handler address that ran, resolved from the vector table at delivery when the schedule named a vector.

resume.description: The address it interrupted, which is where the handler returned.

interrupts_total.description: Deliveries the run made before the cap.

custom_chips.description: The custom-chip configuration this call ran under, as normalization resolved it. Absent when none was asked for. The record says what drew the pixels: a response carrying the bytes and not the chipset would be a picture nobody could reproduce.

dma.description: Absent under shadow mode, where it had no effect: reporting a policy that did not apply would be a claim.

maximum_words.description: Absent under shadow mode, for the same reason as dma.

blits.description: The blits the run performed or refused, capped. A refused blit is here too, and that is the point: the failure this reporting exists to remove is an incomplete picture that nothing reported.

index.description: Position in the run, counting refused blits.

width.description: Words per row, decoded from BLTSIZE, where a field of zero means 64.

height.description: Rows, decoded from BLTSIZE, where a field of zero means 1024.

initial_pointers.description: The A, B, C and D channel pointers when the blit was triggered.

final_pointers.description: And afterwards. Equal to initial_pointers when the blit was refused: a blit that did not happen cannot have advanced a pointer.

datapath_words.description: width times height: what the blit cost the budget, whether or not it ran.

words_written.description: Words the destination channel wrote. Zero when USED was clear or the blit was refused.

zero.description: BZERO: whether every word the datapath produced was zero. Absent when no blit ran, because reporting false there would be a claim.

dma_assumed.description: Whether the blit ran with DMACON saying blitter DMA was off.

refused.description: Why the blit did not run, if it did not.

message.description: For a reader. A consumer reads the structured fields beside it.

observations.description: What is true about this blit that a reader needs in order to distrust the right pixel. Needs no cap: it is bounded by the number of things one blit can be unusual about.

kind.description: A stable name for what was observed: ecs_register_written, reserved_control_bit, both_fill_modes, fill_without_descending, destination_overlaps_source, immediate_data_shift_changed.

register.description: The register offset it is about, when it is about one.

channel.description: The blitter channel it is about, when it is about one.

occurrences.description: How many times it happened. Run-level observations are aggregated by (kind, register) rather than accumulated, so a program writing one register in a loop is one row with a count rather than a million rows.

blits_total.description: Blits triggered, refused ones included. Always the true total, so a capped list never reads as a short run.

attempted_blit_words_total.description: Datapath words every triggered blit asked for, refusals included: what the budget was charged. Refusals are charged because the preflight that refuses one is itself proportional to the blit.

executed_blit_words_total.description: Datapath words the blits that actually ran performed. Two named fields rather than one described as both, so a run that spent its budget on refusals is legible as exactly that.

chip_observations.description: Run-level chip observations, aggregated by kind and register. Bounded by construction: a finite key means a program writing one register in a loop cannot grow this list.

kind.description: A stable name for what was observed: ecs_register_written, reserved_control_bit, both_fill_modes, fill_without_descending, destination_overlaps_source, immediate_data_shift_changed.

register.description: The register offset it is about, when it is about one.

channel.description: The blitter channel it is about, when it is about one.

occurrences.description: How many times it happened. Run-level observations are aggregated by (kind, register) rather than accumulated, so a program writing one register in a loop is one row with a count rather than a million rows.
